utterances.text: And were you ever given a copy of your statement for you to sign and to read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On that same day or later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did you sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this is a -- who gave you a copy of the statement, the officers of Republika Srpska, Ministry of Internal Affairs, or the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor's Office, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Therefore, let's make this clear. You made statements, you gave statements on two occasions; once to the Office of the Prosecutor and once to the officers of Republika Srpska, Ministry of the Internal Affairs; is that correct? On two separate occasions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Office of the Prosecution, did they give you a copy of your statement and ask you to sign it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, the officers of the Republika Srpska Ministry of Internal Affairs, did they give you your statement and ask you to sign it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They gave it to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically we should have two statements signed by you; one which was given to you by the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska and one by the Office of the Prosecutor. You signed twice, in other words; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, going back to the interview you had with the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska, do you remember saying to the person who was interviewing you that you stayed in prison for two days and then you went to sleep at some Behara's apartment. Do you remember saying this to the person who interviewed you from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska? Witness, did you hear my question? My question was: Do you at any time during the interview you had with the officer from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska tell him that you spent in prison the first two days, and then I went to sleep in some Behara's apartment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, in other words, what is included in this statement, in this document, is -- you never mentioned. I didn't hear your answer. Is it a lie? Is it invented by the person who prepared this statement, or is it a reflection of your own words, and you have now forgotten all about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have forgotten. This is not correct. I spent that entire time in prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know a certain Behara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you remember mentioning to the person who interviewed you from the Ministry of Internal Affairs the names of the cooks, Mirfeta, Zumra, and Jaca, and as well as that of Zele? Or is this invented too, in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those names are not invented. These are people I heard about and saw, because they brought us food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So did you mention to the person who interviewed you from the Ministry of Internal Affairs the names of Stojanka from Vizovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this is invented by the person who drew up this statement? I'm trying to get you to help us, Ms. Trifunovic, because we want to make sure whether this statement is reliable or not. Did you ever mention the name Stojanka from Vizovici to the person who was drawing up this statement? And if you didn't, how do you account for the fact that it is included in this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't mention that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Milena and Stana Mitrovic. Did you mention the names of Milena Mitrovic and Stana Mitrovic to the person who was interviewing you from the person from Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you mention the name of Milenija to the person who was interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you mention the name Milka from Kusic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you mention the name of Andja from Novo Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this is also included here, even though you did not mention her name; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you know Andja -- did you meet there Andja from Novo Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever heard that name before, Andja, from Novo Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you aware of any other woman in Srebrenica, in the prison in Srebrenica when you were kept also, that had already been there for four or five months? Try to remember, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear your question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am so sorry. Were you aware that there was at least one woman in the prison with you in Srebrenica that had already been there in the prison for four or five months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you mention the name of Danica from Kusic to the interviewer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you remember mentioning the name Dostana from Bjelovac to the interviewer. This Dostana had with her her daughter-in-law and two children.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. In that prison where I was, there weren't any such people. There might have been there before I arrived or after I had left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Do you remember mentioning the name of Jelka to the interviewer, a certain Jelka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you remember mentioning an older woman with grey hair? But there was no name mentioned here. Do you remember telling the interviewer about another woman, an old woman, an elderly woman, with grey hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you remember mentioning to the interviewer a certain Mico?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you remember mentioning to the interviewer Ilija from Cosici -- Kosici or Cosici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you remember mentioning Stanko from Kusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At this point I give her back to you. It was important for us, Mr. Jones and Mr. Di Fazio, since the witness is not present here in the courtroom, a question of conduct, demeanour, et cetera, becomes important.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm much obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The last question, before I pass her over. You told me that apart from the copy of the statement that you signed for the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, you were also given a copy of the interview or the statement you made to Republika Srpska Ministry of Internal Affairs and that you signed that as well. Do you have a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When I was in Belgrade on the 16th of January, yes, I was given a copy, but not after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who gave you a copy of it on the 16th of January?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 16th of January, no one gave me anything. But rather now, on the 16th, when I was there, in November, when I was in Belgrade, that's when they gave me one. But not before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now when I came to Belgrade for an interview, the 16th of November, they gave me a photocopy. But before when I was in Bosnia and before I got married, no one gave me anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Though I did sign some things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's for the purpose of -- I don't think we can get further than this, unless we can get a clarification from you, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I have questions in re-examination, and I will cover all of these. We certainly intend to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Thank you. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I just say, Your Honour, that we certainly have not received that document signed by Ms. Trifunovic. We found it by our own devices, and that may be a matter which we need some strong -- I'll make some strong marks about subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll see. I mean, the pleasure is yet to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just two final matters. Firstly, could this be given a Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This is being tendered and admitted in evidence and marked as Defence Exhibit D -- what's the next number, 81? D81. Thank you. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just one final question, Ms. Trifunovic. In response to a question by His Honour as to whether you knew Behara, you said no, you don't know Behara; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You don't know Behara.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You've also told us how you were in Belgrade recently, on the 16th of November of this year. Do you recall that you were proofed by the Office of the Prosecutor in relation to this case?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you recall saying to the Prosecutor, and I quote, or I summarise: "I spent one night at Behara's place in Jadar, prior to being exchanged."

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that, and that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So a moment ago when you said you didn't know Behara, that was simply not true.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: I had not known her before that time. I had never seen her or met her. I had never even heard of her before I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jones, and thank you for the cooperation that you have provided, because situations can become very difficult sometimes, and I appreciate your cooperation and your help. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, let's deal with Behara, shall we? You met Behara in Jadar, just before you were exchanged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You had never met her before that; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Have you ever met her since?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. So you don't know Behara, but you met someone called Behara for one night, prior to your exchange; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But I had never heard of or seen a person named Behara before I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at the statement that you were asked questions about -- well, let me rephrase that. Can you please look at the piece of paper that's been marked as D81.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if it's necessary for my learned friend to adopt this rather abrasive and style of referring to it's a piece of paper. It's a Defence Exhibit, and if Mr. Di Fazio would be courteous enough to refer to it as such then that would help --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will decide whether it's just a piece of paper or whether it's a statement or isn't because it's not signed by her. It's purported to be a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Official note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So no arguments in the presence of the witness, please. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Look at the official note, D81, that you have before you. At the bottom there appears to be a signature. Is that your signature? At the bottom there appears to be a signature. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is she seeing this document, just to start with? MR. DI FAZIO: I asked her to be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that you have this document in front of you, Ms. Trifunovic, because from here I cannot verify that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have it in front of me. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And could you then read out to me, at the top right corner, there are -- there is a number, starting with an RR. Could you read out that number to me, please. Top right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you read it out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 321946.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Go ahead, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, please look at that document that His Honour just asked you about. Go down to the bottom of the page --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may. I'm sorry to rise to my feet. But in circumstances where the Prosecution has apparently presented this document to the witness and she signed it and adopted it as hers, this method of proceeding, of showing that a signature, which doesn't purport to be hers anyway, it's obviously the signature of the person who took the note, isn't hers. To make a great demonstration, but it's not her statement. We know it's in the note, but apparently the Prosecution has taken -- has actually shown it to her and she's signed it. And we haven't been provided with a copy of the document. And frankly it's scandalous the way the Prosecution is treating this document, which is from their own file. It's from the rules of the road file. So really, Your Honour, I object to this manner of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. We do need -- I didn't put the question myself because it really wasn't my business, but I think the Prosecution has every right to make sure that this signature here is not the witness' signature, which would confirm, then, that this statement was made or was drawn up as a note of an interview by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, but may I assist that we be provided with a copy of the document, this document, as presented to Ms. Trifunovic and signed by her in Belgrade, and never to this day disclosed to the Defence. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm talking about D81.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But this was apparently presented to her and she signed it in Belgrade when proofed by Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we are talking of D81, the same document that you just tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Indeed. Apparently, she signed it when it was shown to her by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry, I lost my place. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, is that your signature at the bottom of the page of D81?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Look at it. Look at it, Ms. Trifunovic. Just look at the document, at the bottom of the page. Look at the signature. Look at the writing there. Put your eyes -- run your eyes over the handwriting and listen carefully to my question. It's a very simple question. Look at the writing at the bottom of the page. Now, my question is this, very simple: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, when you gave this statement, when you gave this statement, was your mother present?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where was she?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You were, in February of 1993 - I don't want to mislead you; I think Mr. Jones pointed out - 11 and a half; is that correct? 11 and a half years old in 1993, February; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber how it was that you made your way to the police station, or wherever it was that you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: The police took me there, to the police station at Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And if they took you there, where was your mother at that time?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: She was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall if she asked to come along with you?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: They said there was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Could you look at the statement again, please. Mr. Jones pointed out to you portions of the statement where you said that you were not in prison. Do you recall his questions on that? Do you recall his questions about that topic?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In one -- towards the end of your statement, you say -- not at the very end, about four-fifths of the way down, you said words to this effect: "I could move around freely, and then I saw them beating men." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever see men beaten anywhere other than in prison, or hear mean beaten anywhere other than in prison, in the cells that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. I only heard that in prison while I was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours would just bear with me for a moment. I understand that the Registry has the Office of the Prosecutor's statement in the Registry -- in the location at which this witness is now placed, and I would ask that it be produced to her, in particular the front page of the statement. That's the Office of the Prosecutor's statement taken on the 22nd and the 23rd of July, 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any objection to that, Mr. Jones? I suppose not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. We, in fact, arranged for it to be available to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I want to make sure that Mr. Siller is making this document available to the witness. And just to -- for the record, yes, if we could zoom out in a way in which we could at least see on the monitor a glimpse of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Belgrade] Your Honours, I can confirm that the witness has the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Question to Mr. Siller: Mr. Siller, does the witness have this document in front of her? Is the document that we are seeing on the monitor the document that we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Belgrade] Your Honours, I can say that we have shown her the document in B/C/S. She has it in front of her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm afraid, if Your Honours please, it's not the document in B/C/S that I want. It's the English version, if the English version is there. Because the document in B/C/S won't be signed

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question is going to be on the signature, obviously. Mr. Siller, please give the witness a copy of the English text of this statement and not the one in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Belgrade] Your Honours, the witness now has the English copy. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if it is necessary or possible - I don't know whether technically we can do this - because I had -- you have actually basically anticipated what I was going to do. If we could have on the ELMO here juxtaposed the signature that appears on the statement to the Prosecutor and the signature on the statement, let's call it statement, which is now D81 in the B/C/S version, if we could have them on the ELMO and make sure that the witness can see both of them, and if you could enlarge both signatures, it would even make it easier for all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two concerns I have about this. Firstly, Ms. Trifunovic was 11 years old when she signed this. That's one matter. But more fundamentally, Mr. Di Fazio has a copy of this document, as I understand it, in the Prosecutor's possession, which he presented to the witness and which she signed when he was in Belgrade. We should see that signature surely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. We'll probably see that, too. But I assure you, Mr. Jones, that neither you nor myself nor anyone else, including Mr. Di Fazio, anticipated that this was the signature of the witness. I mean, that is the last thing, I think, that all of us, or any one of us could have thought. So at this point in time, once the witness has stated twice, at least, that this is her signature, I mean, obviously it begs the other question of why she has two signatures, one in Cyrillic and one which is not in Cyrillic, and why they present themselves so different, the one from the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Certainly. It's just to say that we should see the signed copy recently signed by the witness which the Prosecution has and hasn't disclosed to us. MR. DI FAZIO: Unless I'm labouring -- I'm not trying to argue here at all, but I just want to understand where Mr. Jones gets that notion from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because purportedly that has a third signature. And we will look into that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It came from her evidence. She said that when she met the Prosecutor in Belgrade, she had been shown this document and signed it again. This document is referred to in the proofing notes of Mr. Di Fazio. No doubt Mr. Di Fazio presented this document to the witness, she signed it, adopted it, and we never received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You are perfectly right, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's what I'm complaining of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're perfectly right. And if there is a signature, an additional signature on that document, we want to see it. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand that. And I now understand what Mr. Jones is -- the point that he is making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question is you're too slow today, Mr. Di Fazio, because I understood Mr. Jones much -- MR. DI FAZIO: Because I can tell Your Honours that I will be unable to produce anything signed by this witness to the Defence in Belgrade recently. If I had, it would be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, in other words, are you stating that she never signed again this document? MR. DI FAZIO: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So there you are, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was presented to her, and it's clear for the proofing notes. And she said today that she had signed it, so it's a matter of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll ask her again. Anyway, let me see on the ELMO the two signatures juxtaposed, please. Is it technically impossible? Usher, I am pretty sure there is -- what is the problem? Put them next. No. Why are you complicating it so much? If you put this part next to this part, you have the two -- MR. DI FAZIO: May I approach and assist the usher?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. You then have them one next to the other. And put them in the center, please. And let's have the technicians -- no, you put them -- approach them, the one to the other, as much as you can, please. We don't need to see the words "signature" and "date." So lift that up, lift it up, further up. No, one next to the other. Lift and put them in the center, please. All right. A little bit further to the left, if you can. Yes. That should be enough. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. And, first of all, I want to make sure that Ms. Trifunovic can see this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Belgrade] Yes, she can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm told there may be problems on the other side. The witness can see what we have on the monitor now. What I suggest is the following: Now that even Mr. Siller has seen the two signatures that we are talking about on the monitor, could he please put the two signatures juxtaposed, one next to the other, in front of the witness, because we are going to ask her questions on these two signatures. I want to make sure, a confirmation from Mr. Siller himself, that he has done so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Belgrade] Your Honours, I can confirm that the witness can now see the same ELMO picture that you can see on the screen, and that the witness on her desk here has both paper copies with the signatures next to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Siller. So, Mr. Di Fazio, she's all yours. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Trifunovic, you now have two documents with some signatures on them. Do you recognise those signatures, or any of those signatures?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you point to --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Can you point to your signature with your finger? Point. Point to it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Your signature or signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. To be a judge, you have to have a gift from God, and that's patience and restraint. How are we going to see now where she is going to point? Can you tell me, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: I can't. It's the limitations of technology. If she were here, of course, it would not happen. So what I'll suggest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll take it one by one. She has seen. They are going to move the camera, focus it on the two documents, and hopefully she will have a pointer and hopefully we will have the cameras zoom in enough for us to be able to see. Still we are seeing her hand with a pointer. MR. DI FAZIO: Can I suggest that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a simpler way of doing it. She has now seen the two signatures juxtaposed; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's being complicated unnecessarily. Now, let's take one of them. Ms. Trifunovic, hold it in your hands, upright, so that the camera can zoom into it so that we know exactly which of the signatures we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Keep that document in your hand, turn it towards you, turn it towards you. Yes. How many signatures do you see on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One. Whose signature is that; do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Take the other document, please, in your hands now. Yes, thank you. Turn it around, turn it towards you. Turn it towards you, please. How many signatures do you see on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you show me that document again, please, facing the camera? Can you turn it facing the camera, and can the camera focus on the bottom part of that document, please. Bottom part of that document. Yes, okay. Can you turn it back towards you, Ms. Trifunovic, please. Yes, I am going to put to you that in that bottom part of that page, there are three signatures, one in Cyrillic and two in Latin script; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So there are three signatures.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is any one of those three signatures yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, all three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean, all three? I see, for example, at the extreme left, I see a signature of a certain Eileen Gillies, Eileen P. Gillies. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two of these are mine, and one isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which ones are yours? Can you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two are mine. This one's mine and this one isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one is yours, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where my finger is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And -- yes. And on the other side of the page, there are two other signatures, with a date. Are any of those other two signatures yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one is not mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the one underneath, the one below it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One is and one isn't mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one that I'm pointing at is mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And which is the other one which is also yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've shown already. This one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But on that document that you have in your hand, apart from that signature that you are showing with your finger now, is there any other signature on that page which is also yours? On that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are two signatures here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Trifunovic, it seems to me that there are three signatures there, not two. Look at the page carefully. Turn the document towards your face. Let's start from the left. There is a signature there which says Eileen P. Gillies; do you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Below it, below it, there is another signature of someone else, probably of Ivana Vencl. Do you see that other signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one isn't, no. One of them is and one of them isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one is yours, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one is and this one isn't, like I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the record, the witness indicates the signature on the right-hand side, which is in Cyrillic. Can you explain to me, therefore, one thing: Do you have two signatures, two signatures? One in Cyrillic and one in Latin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I know I haven't made your life easy today. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful, Your Honour, for your clarifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you always have two signatures, even at the age of -- let me withdraw that. How long have you had two signatures?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Since about four or five years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Well, I think we'll leave the topic of signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would suggest -- I would totally agree with you, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just one other issue that I want to ask you about. You were asked about whether you saw anyone beating the men. You said you didn't see them. In the time that you were in custody, did you ever see --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that, but I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I know. I heard your evidence and I understand that. In the time that you were in custody, when you were being taken from the women's cell to the lavatory, did you ever see anyone other than the Muslim guards that you have spoken about?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: While I was in detention, I did not see any of the men, but I did hear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm asking about when you were being taken from the women's cell to the lavatory, to the bathroom, to the toilet. When you were making those little trips from your cell to the toilet, did you see any men other than, apart from, Muslim guards, the ones you've told us about? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps -- would you like to repeat it or move on. It's up to you, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm going to leave it, and I'm going to complete my re-examination, if Your Honours please. Thank you very much, Ms. Trifunovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are soon finished with you, Ms. Trifunovic, so it's another couple of minutes, and then you can -- you are free to go. Judge Eser would like to put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Ms. Trifunovic, we had a talk about the statement of February 1993, and you told us that the signature on this statement is yours. Now, my question is --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, my question is: Before you signed this document, did you -- have you read it, or was it read to you?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: It was read to me recently, on the 16th, when I went to Belgrade for an interview. But before I was even married, while I was still living in Bosnia, it was never read to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, am I correct in assuming that in the Serbian language mostly is not written in Latin but in Cyrillic; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, at the time of 1993, when you have been 11 and a half years old, have you been able to read Latin, statements written in Latin script, written in Latin?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: I was able to read both, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One last question: What was the size or the measurements of the room, prison cell, that you were kept in in Srebrenica, if you can give us an indication.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question. I don't think I heard you correctly. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. My question is: Could you give us an indication of the size of the room, the prison cell, in Srebrenica where you were kept, together with the other 19 or 20 women? How big or small was it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: That room was quite big. It was a large room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And was it bigger than the room where the men were being kept?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA TRIFUNOVIC
utterances.text: Same size.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same size, okay. Thank you. That completes your testimony, Ms. Trifunovic. I am sure that you are glad to hear that. On behalf of the Tribunal, and on behalf, also, of Judge Brydensholt from Denmark, Judge Eser from Germany, and on my own behalf as Presiding Judge in this trial, I should like to thank you for having accepted to give evidence in this trial. I hope that the arrangements that we made for you have not caused you any undue discomfort or problems. We tried our best. Once more, I thank you, and I can assure you that the staff that we have over there will continue to assist you to make your return to your home as easy as possible. Thank you once more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything else before we adjourn?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Nothing with this witness, Your Honour, but I would want to return to an issue which arose this morning, briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. I want to make sure that the connection with Belgrade is terminated here. And we can proceed. This is something which is not going to take us much time, I suppose, because otherwise we'll have -- we have already gone beyond the break time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, just five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that there's no objection on your part if we sit for another five minutes or so and then we adjourn? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's simply this: My reading of the evidence of Ms. Trifunovic was that she was shown a copy of the document which was -- which became D81 by the Office of the Prosecutor, specifically Mr. Di Fazio, on the 16th of November, 2004, and moreover, that she signed that statement. And I might be wrong about that, but certainly when I read, it's at page 44 of the transcript, Your Honour asked whether she remembered being interviewed by someone from the Republika Srpska Ministry. So that's the 1993 statement; yes. On that occasion, did you make a statement; yes. Was it put in writing; yes. And then further down: Were you given a copy of your statement; yes. Did you sign the statement; yes. And who gave you the statement to sign? Ministry of Affairs [sic] or somebody from the Prosecutor's Office; the Prosecutor's office. I also, and I could again be wrong, but understand it to be the Prosecution's policy that when they present documents to witnesses, they have the witness sign it. Now in light of my learned friend's re-examination today, if it's right that they went to Belgrade with this document, which I insist on emphasising we were not provided with under Rule 66(A)(ii), we found it ourselves and translated it ourselves, which is already a breach of that rule; but if on top of that the Prosecutor showed Ms. Trifunovic this statement and she largely adopted it, by her comments, and maybe even signed it, to then not disclose that statement to us and then suggest in re-examination that a document is a mere piece of paper, with no value, as Mr. Di Fazio is doing, is, in my submission, entirely improper. So I do think that calls for an answer from the Prosecution as to why they didn't disclose this document to us, firstly. Secondly, why, only at the break today, did Mr. Di Fazio even mention this note, which fortunately we had found by our own diligence. And thirdly, if she did sign the statement, why we weren't provided with a copy of the signed statement, a signed version of the official note. Those are all questions which, in my submission, are serious and deserve an answer from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. First of all, may I ask this: RR321946 originates from? MR. DI FAZIO: It's a rules of the road file, which is why it has RR there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, please. MR. DI FAZIO: First of all, there is no policy that Mr. Jones refers to about presentation of documents for signature by witnesses during the proofing process. Each Prosecutor, each lawyer, depending on where they come from, has a different style, a different approach to proofing. For the second time today, I informed Mr. Jones, as I did earlier, that there was no signed version by Ms. Trifunovic which I obtained in Belgrade last week while I was proofing her, and when I presented this document. So I repeat for the second time: No, there is no such document. Mr. Jones may choose or not choose to believe me, but I'm telling the Trial Chamber there is no signed version. So I hope that makes my position clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Disclosure now. MR. DI FAZIO: Disclosure. If I had the document here, and given the evidence that was coming up today, the first thing I would have done was make it available for everyone to see so that we could get to the bottom of this forensic issue. That might have indicated that I should have disclosed it, but I had no document that I could show you, the Trial Chamber, or Defence that was signed by this witness last week when I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You certainly had it last week, because you wouldn't have shown it to the witness in the first place. MR. DI FAZIO: I think what's happening is we're talking at cross-purposes. The document was disclosed to the Defence quite a long time ago as part of the rules of the road file, as part of the rules of the road files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what we want to know. MR. DI FAZIO: That's what I disclosed. But I keep hearing from Mr. Jones the notion that I took this document, RR321946, showed it to this witness last week in Belgrade and got her to sign it, so that we have a recent specimen of her signature. Now, if that is what is being put by Mr. Jones, that did not occur. Secondly, disclosure of this document occurred quite some time ago, as part of a rules of the road --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have a record of it? MR. DI FAZIO: We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't expect you to tell me now. But what we want to make sure of is that this was, indeed, disclosed, and not hidden from the Defence, because the indication that we have from Mr. Jones is that they came across it just by chance, through their own diligence, and not because it was -- it had been disclosed to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, that's correct. If I may assist, as far as that's concerned, we received rules of the road material. We received four boxes of rules of the road material without any list or anything of that nature, and essentially it was a bulk disclosure of rules of the road files. Quite separately from that, the Prosecution has an obligation under Rule 66(A)(ii) to disclose prior statements of Prosecution witnesses. Mr. Di Fazio, clearly on the 16th of November this year, was in Belgrade, he showed that very document to Ms. Trifunovic. It wasn't until the break today that he asked us whether we had it or not. As I say, we happened to have it because we found it amongst four boxes of documents which were not listed, and the question put to me by Mr. Di Fazio indicates that he didn't know whether we had the statement or not. He didn't know. So there's no question of deliberate disclosure of Ms. Trifunovic's past statement to us. MR. DI FAZIO: I asked that question because the case manager raised the issue with me. I was informed before I went to Belgrade that it had been disclosed. And I was checking to make sure, to make sure that my clear understanding was not wrong, to make sure that the Defence had it, to make sure that they weren't about to embark on their cross-examination without having this particular document, as I had been under the impression that it was been disclosed to them. I was making sure that he had it, and that's why I approached Mr. Jones and asked him: Do you have the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did this exchange take place? MR. DI FAZIO: Before the cross-examination commenced by Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: After examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, today. MR. DI FAZIO: Today. I'm told by my case manager that the documents that -- in which they received the statement from Svetlana Trifunovic, the one that we've been talking about, were both inspected by the Defence and then later disclosed to them. I can give you -- later I can give you details of when the document was disclosed to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But there is a difference between a document which is just part of the rules of the road bulk and a document which is, in itself, a statement made by a prospective witness, or a witness that you intend to bring forward, because that is specifically and separately covered or dealt with by the rules. I mean, I don't see why, for example, at the same time you disclosed to the Defence the statement of the witness to the Office of the Prosecutor of July of 2000, you did not also disclose the statement that she had made or the record of the interview she had had with the officer of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska. MR. DI FAZIO: I can't answer that question off the top of my head, if Your Honours please, because I don't know precisely when the OTP statement was disclosed to you. I can let you know. I can get to the records --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not to us, to them. I'm not interested about disclosure to us because, strictly speaking, it's -- you're not required to disclose to us -- MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry, my apologies, to the Defence. I meant to say to the Defence, not to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm going to stop the debate now on this. I take it that you will make your own inquiries about this -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'll get all the information and put it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because the rules, as they are, require proper disclosure and complete disclosure. As regards -- I mean, different kinds of disclosures. As regards witnesses you intend to bring forward, there's a specific rule which I don't need to refer you to because I'm pretty sure you know it by heart by now, and we -- I do want an explanation. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I'll look into the records, and I'll inform you of when these documents were provided to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, it's a very valid point that Judge Brydensholt has now. Who would have done the translation of the original, from the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We did that. That was our own translation, done in Sarajevo, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow. Now, tomorrow we have got a very specific agenda. There is Ms. Manas, who will be testifying. We want to see, since you raised the matter last time, the video relating to the witness that we've had here already, the relevant part of the video, to put us in a better position when we come to decide about that witness. And this, if you can deal with tomorrow, this particular matter that we've been dealing with now. MR. DI FAZIO: There will be no problem with that. In fact, I'd hoped to present the video as part of my submission to you. I'm also arranging for draft translations of what's being said on the video and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right. MR. DI FAZIO: And God willing, they will be available for us all tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And then obviously the debate on the motions. That's all. Thank you. Before we rise, I wish to thank the interpreters, the technicians, everyone here, because we -- but the compensation is that we are finishing earlier today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 26th day of November, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.40 p.m.,
